newsitem.title: USA: Tiffany cites higher sales, operating margin.
newsitem.headline: Tiffany cites higher sales, operating margin.

text.p: Tiffany & Co cited strong worldwide sales growth and a higher operating margin for its higher third quarter earnings, which topped analysts' estimates by $0.02 a share.
The jeweler and specialty retailer said it earned $0.26 a share for the period, compared to $0.19 last year.
Tiffany said U.S. retail sales climbed 14 percent to $99.7 million in the quarter, and same-store sales in the United States rose 9.0 percent.
For the year-to-date, U.S. same-store sales rose 11 percent.
Tiffany Chief Financial Officer James Fernandez told Reuters the company's operating margin rose to 8.8 percent of sales in the third quarter, compared with 6.3 percent a year earlier.
International retail sales rose 11 percent to $88.7 million.

The sales growth rate in Japan was cut by the weakening yen. Total sales in local currency rose 22 percent for both the third quarter and year-to-date. Same-store sales rose six percent in the third quarter and nine percent in the year-to-date.
Sales at Tiffany's Tokyo flagship store were strong, and Sales growth was also healthy in other Asia-Pacific markets as well as Europe and Canada, the company said.
Direct marketing sales grew 8.0 percent to $22.5 million in the third quarter, Tiffany said. Catalog sales grew strongly and corporate sales to U.S. businesses were up modestly.
Tiffany shares closed at 38-1/8 on Wednesday.
